title: Where are the arms and the vertex in a pair of scissors?
description: A pair of scissors is opened and closed by turning its two blades. The blades are drawn as rays, and the point where they are joined is found. Keeko's doubt, that the vertex is where the blades cut, is broken by the cutting place that moves along the blades while the screw stays still.
teaching_notes: One idea: the blades that turn are the arms, and the screw they turn about is the vertex. Watch for students who pick the place where the cutting happens as the vertex.

source: A pair of scissors has two blades. When we open them (or 'turn them') to cut something, the blades form an angle. Identify the arms and the vertex of the angle.
video_script.why: The child finds the arms and the vertex of the angle that the blades of scissors make when they are turned.
video_script.substitution: Draw each blade of the scissors as a ray that starts at the screw.
video_script.anchor: a pair of scissors with two blades, opened to form an angle
video_script.wrong_answer: the vertex is where the blades cut
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says the vertex is where the blades cut because that is where the cutting happens. The cutting place is shown in three different places while the screw stays at one place, so the bubble is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: The blades are the arms, and the vertex is the screw where they are joined

final_answer.value: The two blades are the arms, and the vertex is the screw (pivot) where the blades are joined
final_answer.spoken: the two blades are the arms, and the vertex is the screw, or pivot, where the blades are joined

never_show: the screw named as the vertex, before the answer beat
maths_rules: An angle is formed by two rays with a common starting point; the rays are the arms and the starting point is the vertex.
In scissors the two blades turn, so each blade lies along an arm.
The two blades are joined at the screw, so both arms start there and the screw is the vertex.
Slip: the cutting place moves along the blades when the scissors close, so it is not the vertex.
video_script.design: One idea: the blades are the arms and the screw they turn about is the vertex. The scissors stay on the board and open wider and narrower. The wrong idea is that the cutting place is the vertex.
